expected.description:
Open-source (GPL v2) engine for Soldier of Fortune (2000): clean-room, Yamagi Quake II based. Bring your own licensed copy.

License: GPL-2.0

set.shortDescription: Soldier of Fortune through a new engine: widescreen menus, modern rendering, and the same brutal campaign. Bring your own game files.
set.description: openMERC runs the original Soldier of Fortune maps and data in a community-built engine based on Yamagi Quake II. Its widescreen interface, OpenGL renderer and OpenAL audio give the 2000 shooter a cleaner route onto modern PCs without bundling Raven's game files. You must own and install Soldier of Fortune first. The engine is still in development: its original-module mode is more complete than its fully open-source game logic, and openMERC multiplayer works only with other openMERC clients.

installConfig.playbound_installer.note: Requires your own installed Soldier of Fortune data. PlayBound locates a legal copy, copies it into this edition's separate folder, then adds the matching openMERC release. The GOG copy is untested upstream; the Linux build is experimental.

steps.text: Own and install Soldier of Fortune first. The base folder must contain SoF.exe and base/pak0.pak; openMERC includes no original game assets.
Choose Install in PlayBound. It finds or asks for your Soldier of Fortune folder, copies the game into a separate openMERC edition folder, adds the Windows engine release, and launches openMerc.exe.

Copy a legally installed Soldier of Fortune folder from Windows to a case-sensitive Linux filesystem, then choose Install and locate that folder. PlayBound adds the experimental x86_64 engine build; it requires glibc 2.38+.

set.requirements.min: Windows 10/11: 32-bit openMERC client on a 64-bit PC; GPU supporting OpenGL 3.2. Linux: x86_64, glibc 2.38+, OpenGL 3.2; supply original game data from a legal Windows installation. The developer has not published CPU, RAM, VRAM or full-install disk minimums.
set.requirements.recommended: No recommended CPU, RAM, GPU, VRAM or disk specification has been published for openMERC. Optional graphics effects can be switched off in Video settings.
set.requirements.notes: Requires Soldier of Fortune data, not supplied by openMERC. Retail 1.07f was tested upstream; GOG compatibility is untested. The Windows ZIP is 4.54 MB and the Linux archive is 5.29 MB; neither includes the owned game. Linux display, sound, Wayland and fullscreen have not been verified on real hardware by the developer. macOS has no release build.

min.notes: Windows 10/11 runs the 32-bit client on x64. Linux requires x86_64 and glibc 2.38+. Requires separately owned Soldier of Fortune data. CPU, RAM, VRAM and complete install footprint were not published.

set.license: GPL-2.0-or-later engine; original game assets require a licensed copy
set.longDescription:
Soldier of Fortune was never a shy shooter. A doorway opens, someone leans out, and its hit-location system makes every exchange feel nastier than the usual turn-of-the-century corridor fight. openMERC keeps that recognizable campaign and those original maps, but replaces the aging route into them with a community-built engine. It is a new way to run a game you already own, not a free copy of the game.

The immediate change is how the old world fits a current screen. Menus and the HUD have been rebuilt for widescreen resolutions, with type that scales instead of disappearing into a corner. An OpenGL 3.2 renderer handles the original environments and offers optional effects such as bloom, volumetric fog and dynamic lighting. OpenAL handles sound. These additions are switches, not a demand that a 2000 shooter pretend it was made yesterday. If the extra effects get in the way, turn them off.

There are two ways to run the campaign inside openMERC. The default, mode B, uses the project's own engine, game and player modules. All 32 campaign maps load, but enemy behaviour, some scripts and weapon details are still unfinished. Mode A keeps the new engine while using the original game's modules; upstream calls it the more complete campaign today. The two modes do not share compatible saves, so choose deliberately before settling into a long run. This is a work in progress, and it should be approached like one.

The multiplayer side has a similarly clear boundary. An openMERC client can play with an openMERC host or dedicated server. It cannot join an original Soldier of Fortune 1.07f server, and an original client cannot join an openMERC server. That matters when inviting a friend: both players need this edition and their own licensed game data. The old master-service situation is different too; openMERC uses community master servers rather than relying on the vanished GameSpy service.

PlayBound's install flow starts from your own Soldier of Fortune folder and gives openMERC a separate copy. The engine archive itself is small, but it contains no Raven maps, sounds or other proprietary data. Windows is the primary release. A Linux x86_64 archive exists, but the developer labels it experimental and requires a Windows-sourced game-data folder and a current glibc. There is no macOS release to promise.

We like the ambition here: preserving the feel of a famously uncompromising shooter while making its menus, display and network path easier to live with. We also like that the project states its unfinished pieces plainly. Go in for the campaign, the sharp-edged history and the possibility of an openMERC-only match; keep the original installation and your expectations close at hand.
set.whyWePickedIt: We picked openMERC because it gives a paid PC classic a credible modern engine and a living multiplayer path without pretending the original assets are free. Its widescreen work is immediately useful, and its honest list of unfinished campaign logic makes this an edition worth following rather than overselling.
bestFor: Owners who want Soldier of Fortune on a modern widescreen PC
Players curious about a community engine rebuilding both campaign and multiplayer
Friends willing to use matching openMERC clients for a private match
notFor: Anyone expecting a free copy of Soldier of Fortune or its game data
Players who need a bug-free replacement for every original campaign script
Anyone hoping to join original 1.07f multiplayer servers with this client

firstPlaySteps.text: Confirm that your owned Soldier of Fortune installation contains base/pak0.pak. The engine alone cannot run the campaign.

Launch openMERC. Its default mode B uses the new open-source game modules; if an unfinished mission blocks progress, consult the release notes for mode A, which uses the original modules. Saves are not interchangeable between modes.
Use Video settings to choose your resolution and switch optional rendering effects on or off. The 0.2.2 release requires Windows 10/11 and OpenGL 3.2.
Use a case-sensitive filesystem and confirm glibc 2.38+ and OpenGL 3.2. The Linux release is experimental; real-display, audio and fullscreen behaviour still need testing.

multiplayerGamingSteps.text: Make sure every player uses openMERC with their own licensed Soldier of Fortune data. Original 1.07f clients and servers cannot join an openMERC session.
The host starts a match in openMERC or runs its openMerc-ded dedicated binary. Share the server address with friends; guests open Multiplayer in openMERC and connect to that address.
For a PlayBound virtual LAN party, have all members join the party network before hosting or connecting. The game still handles map and match settings.

patchNotes.title: openMERC 0.2.2
patchNotes.body: Windows and experimental Linux archives. Fixes a weapon-drop crash in the open-source game module and adds a text-size control for console, chat and subtitles. See the upstream release for full changes and known issues.

faq.q: Is openMERC a free copy of Soldier of Fortune?
faq.a: No. The engine is open source, but it includes none of the original game assets. You need your own licensed Soldier of Fortune installation; PlayBound uses its files only for your local edition install.

faq.q: Which campaign mode should I use?
faq.a: Mode B uses openMERC's own game and player modules and is the default, but some AI and scripts remain unfinished. Mode A uses the original modules through the new engine and is currently the more complete campaign. Saves from one mode do not load in the other.

faq.q: Can I join original Soldier of Fortune servers?
faq.a: No. openMERC's network protocol is not compatible with original 1.07f servers or clients. Everyone in a match needs openMERC.

The developer documents GOG as a possible legal source but has not tested the current release against it. Retail Soldier of Fortune 1.07f is the tested base. Keep this edition unverified until the GOG path is tried.

faq.q: Which operating systems have downloadable builds?
faq.a: The 0.2.2 release supplies Windows 32-bit and experimental Linux x86_64 archives. It runs on Windows 10/11; Linux requires glibc 2.38+ and a case-sensitive filesystem. There is no current macOS build.

The engine contains SDL3 gamepad input and menu navigation. PlayBound has not yet verified this edition with a physical controller, so keyboard and mouse remain the safe fallback while it is in testing.

set.verificationNote: Upstream 0.2.2 Windows and Linux archives, SHA-256 hashes and file layouts checked against the developer's release. Retail 1.07f is the developer-tested data source; GOG, Linux real hardware, controller behaviour and a live multiplayer session remain untested by PlayBound.
